question: If p(√3 + cot 30°) = tan³60° - 2sin60°, then the value of p is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Substitute the standard trigonometric values directly into the given equation:

⇒ p(√3 + √3) = (√3)³ − 2 × (√3 / 2)

⇒ p(2√3) = 3√3 − √3

⇒ p(2√3) = 2√3

⇒ p = 1

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

p(√3 + cot 30°) = tan³ 60° − 2sin 60°

**Formula Used:**

cot 30° = √3

tan 60° = √3

sin 60° = √3 / 2

**Calculations:**

⇒ p(√3 + √3) = (√3)³ − 2 × (√3 / 2)

⇒ p(2√3) = 3√3 − √3

⇒ p(2√3) = 2√3

⇒ p = 2√3 ÷ 2√3

⇒ p = 1

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Standard Trigonometric Values

• sin 30° = 1/2 | sin 45° = 1/√2 | sin 60° = √3/2
• cos 30° = √3/2 | cos 45° = 1/√2 | cos 60° = 1/2
• tan 30° = 1/√3 | tan 45° = 1 | tan 60° = √3

Key Trigonometric Identities

• sin²θ + cos²θ = 1
• 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ
• 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ

Reciprocal Relations

• cosec θ = 1 ÷ sin θ
• sec θ = 1 ÷ cos θ
• cot θ = 1 ÷ tan θ = cos θ ÷ sin θ
</p
